schemaExtensionNote: This is the first manifest entry for MLC 2006. Unlike ISM (flat numbered Elements, docs/academy/ism-master-source-manifest/) and ISPS (flat numbered Sections, docs/academy/isps-master-source-manifest/), the MLC 2006 Code is vertically integrated into Article / Regulation / Standard (Part A, mandatory) / Guideline (Part B, non-mandatory) tiers grouped by subject. This entry therefore adds three fields not present in the ISM/ISPS manifest schema - regulationRef, standardARef, guidelineBRef - to name each tier explicitly, in addition to the shared fields (sourceId, title, authority, moduleCode, section, fullText, amendmentHistory, verificationMethod, verifiedBy, verifiedAt) already used by ISM/ISPS. This is an additive extension to this docs/ JSON file's own shape only - it does not touch config/human-review-contract.json or any other shared schema/contract file.
verificationMethodNote: This session had no access to the GROK/GEMINI dual-AI cross-check pipeline used in PR #213/#214. Verification here instead used: (1) a direct fetch and local pdftotext -layout extraction of two independently hosted mirrors of the ILO's own original 2006 published Convention text - register-iri.com (Marshall Islands flag registry's copy) and ilo.org/media/269841 (ILO's own hosted copy) - which were diffed against each other for the Title 1 / Regulation 1.1 / Standard A1.1 / Guideline B1.1 block and found byte-for-byte identical; (2) an independent secondary source (edumaritime.net) which paraphrases (not verbatim-quotes) the same provisions and matches on every substantive point (16-year minimum, night-work definition of at least 9 hours starting no later than midnight and ending no earlier than 5 a.m., the two training/duty exception conditions, under-18 hazardous-work prohibition, and the Guideline's 'special attention' wording); (3) a targeted web search across the five MLC amendment rounds (2014, 2016, 2018, 2022, 2025) confirming none of them amended Regulation 1.1, Standard A1.1, or Guideline B1.1 - the amended regulations across all five rounds were 1.4, 2.1, 2.2, 2.4, 2.5, 3.1, 3.2, 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3, never 1.1. This is a two-independent-primary-source-mirror verification plus an independent amendment-history check, not a three-way GROK/GEMINI/primary-source cross-check - documented explicitly as a different method from PR #213/#214 rather than silently presented as equivalent.

verifiedSources.title: Minimum Age
verifiedSources.section: Title 1, Regulation 1.1 / Standard A1.1 / Guideline B1.1
verifiedSources.fullText:
TITLE 1. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS FOR SEAFARERS TO WORK ON A SHIP

Regulation 1.1 - Minimum age

Purpose: To ensure that no under-age persons work on a ship

1. No person below the minimum age shall be employed or engaged or work on a ship.

2. The minimum age at the time of the initial entry into force of this Convention is 16 years.

3. A higher minimum age shall be required in the circumstances set out in the Code.

Standard A1.1 - Minimum age

1. The employment, engagement or work on board a ship of any person under the age of 16 shall be prohibited.

2. Night work of seafarers under the age of 18 shall be prohibited. For the purposes of this Standard, "night" shall be defined in accordance with national law and practice. It shall cover a period of at least nine hours starting no later than midnight and ending no earlier than 5 a.m.

3. An exception to strict compliance with the night work restriction may be made by the competent authority when:
(a) the effective training of the seafarers concerned, in accordance with established programmes and schedules, would be impaired; or
(b) the specific nature of the duty or a recognized training programme requires that the seafarers covered by the exception perform duties at night and the authority determines, after consultation with the shipowners' and seafarers' organizations concerned, that the work will not be detrimental to their health or well-being.

4. The employment, engagement or work of seafarers under the age of 18 shall be prohibited where the work is likely to jeopardize their health or safety. The types of such work shall be determined by national laws or regulations or by the competent authority, after consultation with the shipowners' and seafarers' organizations concerned, in accordance with relevant international standards.

Guideline B1.1 - Minimum age

1. When regulating working and living conditions, Members should give special attention to the needs of young persons under the age of 18.
verifiedSources.variantNote: None identified - the two independently hosted primary-source mirrors used (register-iri.com and ilo.org/media/269841) produced byte-for-byte identical text for this entire block, including punctuation and line structure.
verifiedSources.amendmentHistory: Convention adopted 23 February 2006 (Ninety-fourth Session of the International Labour Conference, convened 7 February 2006); entered into force 20 August 2013. The Code (Parts A and B) has since been amended by the ILO in five rounds - 2014, 2016, 2018, 2022 and 2025 - none of which amended Regulation 1.1, Standard A1.1, or Guideline B1.1. Confirmed via independent web search today of each round's affected-regulations list: 2014 amended Regulations 2.5 and 4.2 (financial security); 2016 amended provisions related to shipboard harassment and bullying guidance; 2018 amended Standards A2.1 and A2.2 (seafarers' employment agreements and wages during piracy captivity); 2022 amended Regulations 1.4, 2.5, 3.1, 3.2, 4.1 and 4.3; 2025 amended Regulations 2.4 and 2.5 and provisions under 1.4. Title 1 / Regulation 1.1 does not appear in any of the five rounds' affected-provisions lists.
